01.name: January
beats: Days 1–6 — Opening movement. Creation, fall, flood, Babel — the Word present before the ruin; the covenant line already forming. Center of gravity: Gen 5; Gen 6:1-12; Gen 6:13-22.
Days 7–12 — Second movement. Abraham called and tested; Job argues with his comforters while God stays silent — for now. Center of gravity: Job 8; Gen 16; Gen 17:1-22.
Days 13–18 — Third movement. Isaac and Jacob — the promise survives famine, deception, and twenty years of Laban. Center of gravity: Job 19; Gen 25; Gen 26.
Days 19–24 — Fourth movement. Joseph sold, imprisoned, and raised; Job’s debate hardens toward the whirlwind. Center of gravity: Job 30; Gen 39; Gen 40.
Days 25–31 — Closing movement. God answers Job; Jacob’s house comes to Egypt; a new king knows not Joseph — the plagues begin. Center of gravity: Jas 5:7-11; Rom 8:18-25; 1 Pet 1:6-9.

ahead.title: January 2026 · Month Ahead
ahead.lede: January opens the Book with the Word already present at creation and walks a man from garden to flood to promise to Egypt’s brink. Creation week to Egypt’s door: Logos over Genesis; flood; patriarchs with Job alongside; Joseph; the plagues begin.
ahead.charge: Enter January awake. Keep all five watches. Honor event time and written time, and let the Word press your household. Carry creation week to Egypt’s door into February without dropping the line.

02.name: February
beats: Days 1–5 — Opening movement. Passover blood, exit night, the sea split, bread from heaven, law from the mountain. Center of gravity: Ex 15:1-21; Ex 15:22-27; Ex 16.
Days 6–10 — Second movement. Covenant ratified; the tabernacle pattern given; the calf, the intercession, the covenant renewed. Center of gravity: Ex 29; Ex 30; Ex 31.
Days 11–15 — Third movement. The tent built exactly as commanded; glory fills it; Leviticus opens at the altar. Center of gravity: Ex 39:1-31; Ex 39:32-43; Ex 40.
Days 16–20 — Fourth movement. Priests ordained; strange fire; clean and unclean — holiness has a floor plan. Center of gravity: Lev 10; Lev 11:1-23; Lev 11:24-47.
Days 21–28 — Closing movement. Atonement, the holiness code, the feasts, Jubilee; then Numbers musters the camp. Center of gravity: Lev 23:1-22; Lev 23:23-44; Lev 24.

ahead.title: February 2026 · Month Ahead
ahead.lede: February is blood, water, fire, and furniture — Passover night through wilderness liturgy. Freedom is not formless; God camps with a people. Blood on the door; sea; Sinai; tabernacle; Numbers musters the camp.
ahead.charge: Enter February awake. Keep all five watches. Honor event time and written time, and let the Word press your household. Carry Passover to wilderness order into March without dropping the line.

03.name: March
beats: Days 1–6 — Opening movement. The camp ordered and blessed; Kadesh refuses the land — forty years decreed. Center of gravity: Num 10:35-11:23; Num 11:24-35; Num 12.
Days 7–12 — Second movement. Aaron dies; the bronze serpent; Balaam blesses what he was hired to curse; the plains counted. Center of gravity: Num 25; Num 26; Num 27.
Days 13–18 — Third movement. Deuteronomy preaches: hear, love, remember — one God, one altar, one people. Center of gravity: Deut 8; Deut 9; Deut 10-11.
Days 19–24 — Fourth movement. Blessings and curses set before them; the Song of Moses; Moses dies in sight of the land; Jordan crossed. Center of gravity: Deut 27-28; Deut 29; Deut 30-31.
Days 25–31 — Closing movement. Jericho to Shechem — the land divided, the covenant renewed, and Judges opens the long forgetting. Center of gravity: Josh 16; Josh 17; Josh 18.

ahead.title: March 2026 · Month Ahead
ahead.lede: March finishes the wilderness sermon and opens the long ache of Judges. Covenant memory is tested the moment the land is nearly in hand. Deuteronomy preaches covenant; Jordan is crossed; the cycles of forgetfulness begin.
ahead.charge: Enter March awake. Keep all five watches. Honor event time and written time, and let the Word press your household. Carry wilderness close to Judges open into April without dropping the line.

04.name: April
beats: Days 1–6 — Opening movement. Deborah’s song, Gideon’s three hundred, Abimelech’s briars — deliverance keeps arriving sideways. Center of gravity: Judg 8:1-21; Judg 8:22-35; Judg 9:1-21.
Days 7–12 — Second movement. Samson’s ruin, Israel’s chaos, Ruth’s hesed; Samuel hears his name in the dark; the ark goes captive. Center of gravity: Judg 21; Ruth 1; Ruth 2.
Days 13–18 — Third movement. A king demanded; Saul crowned, then rejected; a shepherd anointed while Goliath still shouts. Center of gravity: 1 Sam 13; 1 Sam 14:1-23; 1 Sam 14:24-52.
Days 19–24 — Fourth movement. David the fugitive spares the king twice; Saul falls on Gilboa; David crowned at Hebron, then over all Israel. Center of gravity: 1 Sam 28; 1 Sam 29; 1 Sam 30.

Days 25–30 — Closing movement. The ark comes home; the covenant promised to David’s house; Bathsheba, Nathan, Absalom — the sword enters the house. Center of gravity: 2 Sam 8; 1 Chr 18; 2 Sam 9; 1 Chr 19:1-19; 2 Sam 10; 1 Chr 20:1-3.

ahead.title: April 2026 · Month Ahead
ahead.lede: April is the hinge from tribal chaos to monarchy. Kindness still writes genealogy (Ruth) while a nation begs for a king like the nations. Deliverers; Ruth’s hesed; a king requested; a shepherd raised; a house divided in the making.
ahead.charge: Enter April awake. Keep all five watches. Honor event time and written time, and let the Word press your household. Carry Judges through David’s fracture into May without dropping the line.

05.name: May
beats: Days 1–6 — Opening movement. Absalom dies in the wood; David restored, singing; the census sin buys the temple site. Center of gravity: 2 Sam 20:14-26; 2 Sam 21; 2 Sam 22:1-25.
Days 7–12 — Second movement. David orders worship and hands Solomon the plans; the throne secured; wisdom granted; the temple rises. Center of gravity: 1 Kgs 1:1-27; 1 Kgs 1:28-53; 1 Kgs 2:1-25.

Days 13–18 — Third movement. Dedication glory; Sheba’s visit; Song of Songs early, Ecclesiastes late — the wise king’s heart turns. Center of gravity: 1 Kgs 10:14-29; 2 Chr 9:13-28; 1 Kgs 11:1-8; Eccl 1.
Days 19–24 — Fourth movement. The kingdom torn at Shechem; calves at Bethel; Asa’s reforms; Elijah calls down fire on Carmel. Center of gravity: 1 Kgs 15:9-24; 2 Chr 14; 2 Chr 15; 2 Chr 16.

Days 25–31 — Closing movement. Horeb’s whisper; Naboth avenged; Elisha’s double portion; Jehu’s purge; Assyria’s shadow lengthens. Center of gravity: 2 Kgs 8:1-24; 2 Chr 21; 2 Kgs 8:25-9:22; 2 Chr 22:1-9; 2 Kgs 9:23-10:14; 2 Chr 22:10-12.

ahead.title: May 2026 · Month Ahead
ahead.lede: May watches glory and fracture share a calendar — temple gold and divided thrones, wisdom songs and prophetic fire. Absalom’s fallout; Solomon’s glory and late rot; Elijah’s fire on a split kingdom.
ahead.charge: Enter May awake. Keep all five watches. Honor event time and written time, and let the Word press your household. Carry David’s end to divided thrones into June without dropping the line.

06.name: June
beats: Days 1–6 — Opening movement. Ahaz buys an altar; Israel falls to Assyria; Hezekiah cleanses the house and outlasts Sennacherib. Center of gravity: 2 Kgs 18:1-16; 2 Chr 29; Isa 3.
Days 7–12 — Second movement. Manasseh’s long ruin; Isaiah’s throne-room call; Josiah finds the Book — the reform that came too late. Center of gravity: Isa 9; Isa 10; Isa 11.
Days 13–18 — Third movement. Jerusalem falls and Cyrus is already named; Jeremiah called young and told not to fear their faces. Center of gravity: Jer 1; Jer 2:1-22; Jer 2:23-37.
Days 19–24 — Fourth movement. The prophet weeps and the city will not hear; Lamentations closes the nights over the ruins. Center of gravity: Jer 16; Jer 17; Jer 18.

Days 25–30 — Closing movement. Daniel stands in a foreign court — furnace, tree, writing on the wall, lions — while Jeremiah’s scroll is burned and rewritten. Center of gravity: Jer 31:27-40; Jer 32; Jer 33.

ahead.title: June 2026 · Month Ahead
ahead.lede: June is the sound of a city under sentence. Prophets do not decorate the fall; they interpret it while Daniel already stands in a foreign court. Isaiah’s holy vision; kings under Assyria; Jeremiah’s tears; Jerusalem falls.
ahead.charge: Enter June awake. Keep all five watches. Honor event time and written time, and let the Word press your household. Carry prophets before the fall into July without dropping the line.

review.lede: June was the sound of a city under sentence. Prophets do not decorate the fall; they interpret it while Daniel already stands in a foreign court. Isaiah’s holy vision; kings under Assyria; Jeremiah’s tears; Jerusalem falls.

07.name: July
beats: Days 1–5 — Opening movement. Empires fall on paper before they fall in history. Daniel 8–12 seals the end; Jeremiah’s nations scroll ends with Babylon’s doom; Isaiah mocks gods that cannot carry their own statues. Center of gravity: Jer 48:26-47; Jer 49:1-22; Jer 49:23-39.

Days 6–14 — Second movement. Ezekiel’s full arc opens — throne-chariot, watchman, glory departing — while Ezra’s lists, opposition, and finished temple run alongside. Rebuild is holiness with a census roll, not bricks alone. Center of gravity: Ezek 20; Ezek 21; Ezek 22.

Days 15–27 — Third movement. Nehemiah’s wall and the Word (parallel track). Cupbearer to builder; sword and trowel; Torah read until weeping, then feast. The minor prophets preach beside the wall: Joel, Amos, Jonah, Micah, Nahum. Center of gravity: Amos 2; Amos 3; Amos 4.

Days 28–31 — Fourth movement. Esther opens; Habakkuk’s faith, Zephaniah’s day, Haggai’s house, Zechariah’s night visions. God rules trowel and throne room on the same page. Center of gravity: Hab 3; Zeph 1; Zeph 2. Peace track — Peace track — Isaiah’s burden, then Hosea’s heart, then comfort. Many nights close not with a soft psalm but with judgment oracles that still end in hope. That is July’s tone: hard truth, stubborn mercy.

ahead.title: July 2026 · Month Ahead
ahead.lede: July will not babysit you. It will take you from the last visions of a captive prophet to a sleepless Persian king — through Ezekiel, return and rebuild, the minor prophets, and the quiet courage of a Jewish queen. You will start in Babylon’s shadow. You will finish with a hammer in one hand and a decree of death hanging over a people God will not abandon.
ahead.charge: Enter July awake. Empires will fall on the page before they fall in history. Keep the five watches. When dry bones rattle, do not rush past the Word that raises them.

review.title: July 2026 · Month in Review
review.lede: July did not babysit you. It took you from the last visions of a captive prophet to a sleepless Persian king — through the full weight of Ezekiel, the grit of return and rebuild, the thunder of the minor prophets, and the quiet courage of a Jewish queen. You started in Babylon’s shadow. You finished with a hammer in one hand and a decree of death hanging over a people God would not abandon.
review.charge: Do not leave July as a finished checklist. Leave it as a man who has seen empires judged, a temple measured, a wall finished, and a queen step into risk because silence would have been sin. Carry that into August — the Old Testament is about to close its mouth, and the Word is about to become flesh on the page in front of you.

08.name: August
chips: Gospels written later · W c. AD 50–90
beats: Days 1–3 — Opening movement. OT last words. Esther’s climax and Purim; Zechariah’s pierced one and fountain; Malachi’s messenger and sun of righteousness. Then the page turns: two genealogies. The silence after Malachi is not empty — it is pregnant. Center of gravity: Zech 11-12; Zech 13-14; Mal 1.

Days 4–9 — Second movement. Incarnation and early signs. Annunciation; Nativity; baptism under Tiberius; temptation; Cana; Nicodemus; the Samaritan woman; Nazareth’s rejection. The kingdom enters as a Person. Center of gravity: Mt 3; Mk 1:1-11; Lk 3:1-22; Mt 4:1-11; Lk 4:1-13.

Days 10–22 — Third movement. Galilee authority and rising cost. Demons silenced; the paralytic forgiven; the Twelve sent; Sabbath conflict; the Lord’s Prayer; lost sheep, coin, and prodigal. The Son of Man already walks toward a cross while He heals on the way. Center of gravity: Mt 12:1-21; Mt 12:22-37; Mt 12:38-50.

Days 23–29 — Fourth movement. Holy Week compressed. Tears over Jerusalem; entry; temple cleansed; Olivet; virgins, talents, sheep and goats. Chronological, not liturgical — the King rides in while the calendar still says late summer. Center of gravity: Mk 12:1-12; Mk 12:13-27; Mk 12:28-44.

Days 30–31 — Closing movement. Upper Room threshold. Plot; Passover prep; the anointing at Bethany; betrayal priced; foot washing; “I am the way.” You will not finish the Passion in August — you will be positioned inside it, ready for September to continue. Center of gravity: Lk 22:1-23; Lk 22:24-38; Mt 26:6-16; Mk 14:1-11.

ahead.title: August 2026 · Month Ahead
ahead.lede: August is a hinge month. In three days the Old Testament closes its mouth. By the end of the first week the Word has become flesh on the page — birth, baptism, temptation, Cana. By the last week you are already in Passion week, washing feet and hearing “I am the way.” You will start with a gallows prepared for Mordecai. You will finish in an upper room with a towel around the Lord’s waist.
ahead.charge: Enter August awake. The prophets have done their shouting. The genealogies are about to name a Man. Keep the five watches. Keep the dual clocks. When the week turns holy before the month ends, do not rush past the tears over Jerusalem to get to the next checkbox. He is riding toward a cross — and you are riding with the text.

review.charge: Do not leave August as a finished checklist. Leave it as a man who met a King on the page. Carry the dual clocks and the towel-and-table posture into September.

09.name: September
beats: Days 1–6 — Opening movement. Upper Room promises; the high-priestly prayer; Gethsemane, arrest, denial, Pilate — the crucifixion. Center of gravity: Jn 17:13-26; Mt 26:17-30; Mk 14:12-26; Lk 22:39-53.
Days 7–12 — Second movement. “It is finished”; the burial watch; resurrection morning; Emmaus; Thomas; breakfast on the shore. Center of gravity: Jn 20:1-18; Mt 28:1-10; Lk 24:1-12.

Days 13–18 — Third movement. Ascension and Pentecost; the church born praying; boldness before the council; deacons chosen and Stephen seized. Center of gravity: Acts 3:1-10; Acts 3:11-26; Acts 4:1-12.

Days 19–24 — Fourth movement. Stephen’s face like an angel; the scattering preaches; the Damascus road; Cornelius — the Gentiles receive the Spirit. Center of gravity: Acts 9:1-9; Acts 9:10-19; Acts 9:20-31.
Days 25–30 — Closing movement. First journey out and back; Galatians defends the gospel; the Jerusalem Council settles it; the second journey launches. Center of gravity: Acts 14:21-28; Gal 1; Gal 2.

ahead.title: September 2026 · Month Ahead
ahead.lede: September does not let you stay at the table. It takes you through the night, the wood, the stone rolled, the Spirit poured, and the road out of Jerusalem. Passion finished; empty tomb; Pentecost; persecution; Paul called; the gospel to the nations.
ahead.charge: Enter September awake. Keep all five watches. Honor event time and written time, and let the Word press your household. Carry cross to first mission roads into October without dropping the line.

10.name: October
beats: Days 1–6 — Opening movement. Philippi’s jail sings; Thessalonica and Berea; Athens’ unknown god; eighteen months at Corinth — the letters begin to travel. Center of gravity: 1 Thess 3:11-13; 1 Thess 4:1-12; Acts 17:1-9.

Days 7–12 — Second movement. Ephesus — the Word prevails and the silversmiths riot; 1 Corinthians confronts a divided, gifted, messy church. Center of gravity: Acts 19:21-41; 1 Cor 1:1-17; 1 Cor 1:18-31.
Days 13–18 — Third movement. Farewell at Miletus; “ready to die at Jerusalem”; seized in the temple; testimony on the steps. Center of gravity: Acts 21:15-26; 1 Cor 7:17-35; 1 Cor 7:36-40.

Days 19–24 — Fourth movement. Love set in the middle of the gift lists; resurrection argued to the end; 2 Corinthians — treasure in jars of clay. Center of gravity: 1 Cor 14:26-40; 1 Cor 15:1-34; 1 Cor 15:35-49.
Days 25–31 — Closing movement. The collection and the boast of weakness; Sanhedrin, Felix, Festus, Agrippa; storm, shipwreck, Malta. Center of gravity: Acts 24:1-21; Acts 24:22-25:12; Acts 25:13-27.

ahead.title: October 2026 · Month Ahead
ahead.lede: October teaches that doctrine travels. Letters are not a quiet appendix — they are weapons and comfort inside the same missionary storm as Acts. Epistles threaded into Acts; the collection; arrest; shipwreck; Rome on the horizon.
ahead.charge: Enter October awake. Keep all five watches. Honor event time and written time, and let the Word press your household. Carry letters in the storm into November without dropping the line.

11.name: November
beats: Days 1–6 — Opening movement. Ephesians — seated with Christ, walking worthy, standing armed; Philippians — joy from a Roman chain. Center of gravity: Eph 4:1-16; Eph 4:17-32; Eph 5:1-21.
Days 7–12 — Second movement. Colossians — Christ preeminent; Philemon — the gospel crosses a master’s threshold; Romans opens its case. Center of gravity: Col 1:24-2:7; Col 2:8-15; Col 2:16-23.
Days 13–18 — Third movement. No one righteous; justified by faith; buried and raised with Him; no condemnation — the Spirit’s chapter. Center of gravity: Rom 5:12-21; Rom 6:1-14; Rom 6:15-23.

Days 19–23 — Fourth movement. God’s purpose for Israel; living sacrifices; authorities and love owed; the strong bearing with the weak; Phoebe carries the letter. Center of gravity: Rom 13:1-7; Rom 13:8-14; Rom 14:1-12.

Days 24–30 — Closing movement. The ministry core reviewed — Sermon on the Mount, kingdom parables, Transfiguration — then the pastorals: guard the deposit, fight the good fight. Center of gravity: Mt 16:13-28; Mt 17:1-13; Mt 18:1-14, 21-35.

12.name: December
beats: Days 1–5 — Opening movement. Acts ends unchained — the door open; the Son of Man among the lampstands; seven letters; the pastorals swept at speed. Center of gravity: 1 Tim 4; 1 Tim 5; 1 Tim 6.
Days 6–11 — Second movement. The throne and the Lamb; seals and trumpets; Romans re-walked in a single week — the gospel at a run. Center of gravity: Rom 6; Rom 7; Rom 8.
Days 12–17 — Third movement. The dragon and the beasts; the harvest; James through Jude — faith that works, hope that suffers, truth that abides. Center of gravity: 1 Pet 4; 1 Pet 5; 2 Pet 1.
Days 18–25 — Fourth movement. Babylon falls and the King returns; Advent — genealogies, Nativity, the Word made flesh; Christmas Day. Center of gravity: Isa 60:1-12; Isa 60:13-22; Isa 61:1-7.
Days 26–31 — Closing movement. The new city already glimpsed; the Song of Moses; “choose this day”; the year seals in unbroken praise. Center of gravity: Josh 1; Josh 3; Josh 24.
